title: General Lindblad equation for quarkonium evolution in a quark-gluon plasma
authors: Aoumeur Daddi Hammou, Jean-Paul Blaizot, Pol Bernard Gossiaux, Thierry Gousset
abstract: Accurate modelling and understanding of quarkonium production in ultrarelativistic heavy ion collisions requires a formalism that preserves the quantum properties of microscopic $\bar{Q}Q$ systems while treating the interaction of such pairs with the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). The open quantum system approach has recently emerged as one of the most fruitful schemes to meet such requirements. However, the quantum master equations obtained so far in this context are derived assuming a strict ordering between the QGP temperature $T$ and the $\bar{Q}Q$ energy gaps ($ΔE$) of the quarkonia bound states. This limits their predictive power since, as the QGP expands and cools down, the system traverse all regimes between the quantum Brownian motion (QBM) regime for $T\gtrsim ΔE$ to the quantum optical (QO) regime for $ΔE\gtrsim T$. In this paper, we derive and present a more general non-abelian quantum master equation of the Lindblad type, which does not suffer from these limitations and thus allows to faithfully describe the quantum evolution of the $Q\bar{Q}$ pairs during the whole QGP-evolution. We also provide some illustration of the key quantities governing this equation.
summary: The paper addresses the challenge of modeling quarkonium evolution in a QGP by deriving a universal Lindblad master equation. This new formalism overcomes limitations of previous models that could only describe specific temperature regimes. It provides a unified, quantum description for $ ar{Q}Q$ pair dynamics across the entire cooling history of the plasma.
main_problem: Developing a quantum mechanical formalism to accurately model quarkonium ($ ar{Q}Q$) evolution within the Quark-Gluon Plasma (QGP) that remains valid across all temperature regimes.
main_result: The authors derive a general, non-abelian Lindblad master equation (ULE) that unifies descriptions previously restricted to separate Quantum Brownian Motion and Quantum Optical regimes.
method: The derivation uses the Open Quantum System approach, starting from the reduced density matrix evolution and transforming it into a Lindblad form via approximations like Born-Markov.
model_or_system: The system models heavy quark-antiquark pairs interacting with a QGP. The dynamics are governed by a generalized Lindblad master equation that incorporates non-unitary dissipation terms derived from plasma correlators.
key_observables: Quarkonium suppression, spectral functions, and the coupled singlet-octet dynamics of the $ ar{Q}Q$ pair.
important_parameters: The temperature ($T$) relative to the energy gap ($\Delta E$), which dictates the transition between QBM ($T \gtrsim \Delta E$) and QO ($\Delta E \gtrsim T$) regimes.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the Born-Markov approximation, and some intermediate steps assume thermal equilibrium (KMS boundary conditions) or non-relativistic treatment of the heavy quarks.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the focus is on deriving equations and illustrating key quantities like decay rates and spectral density using the derived framework.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the limitations of existing QME approaches (restricted by $T$ vs $\Delta E$) to deriving the general Lindblad form, showing how it unifies descriptions across different physical regimes, and finally illustrating its application via key observables.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it applies advanced open quantum system techniques (Lindblad master equations) to a strongly interacting, non-equilibrium many-body system (QGP), bridging concepts from quantum optics/dissipation theory into high-energy nuclear physics.
